valuation: US duty on FOB value; PT/UK duty on CIF; VAT on CIF+duty
compliance: Preferential rates require GENUINE origin under the agreement's rules of origin (product-specific rules, e.g. yarn-forward for apparel under USMCA/CAFTA-DR, double transformation under EU/UK GSP/EBA).
Claim preference with the required proof: certificate of origin / statement on origin (REX number for EU/UK GSP), USMCA certification of origin; keep supplier declarations and production records.
Transshipment or relabeling to change apparent origin is customs fraud (e.g. 19 U.S.C. 1592; EU OLAF / UK HMRC enforcement) with penalties, seizure and criminal liability.
Paying the seller in crypto does NOT change duty or VAT: customs value is the transaction value converted to local currency at the official customs exchange rate.
Not legal or tax advice; confirm with a licensed customs broker before importing.

notes: No customs tariff or import VAT applies in orbit: space is not a customs territory. Duties/VAT can still apply when goods are imported into the launch country (e.g. shipping a satellite from abroad to a US launch site) and on anything returned to Earth: check source.

Export controls are NOT computed: spacecraft and related items may be controlled under ITAR (USML Cat. XV) or EAR (CCL, e.g. 9A515); launching from or exporting to another country can need a license. Also launch/spectrum licensing (FAA/FCC or national equivalents). Get export-control counsel.
Paying in crypto does not change any of this.

crypto: Seller-accepts-crypto filter is a placeholder: no seller data yet, so no route is excluded. Crypto payment does not change duty or VAT (customs value is converted to local currency).
